adjudication_anchor: Table 3 and §4 experimental results; benchmark setup describing 13 tasks and all repeated trials
adjudication_rationale: The paper reports host metrics over all 728 realized trials and analyzes traces from all runs. Because failures remain in the trial accounting, the initiated-run denominator is recoverable; whether the endpoint is scientific validity is a separate R4 question.

adjudication_anchor: Appendix F.7, especially the statement that 7 tasks × 8 runs yield 56 trajectories; failure-handling appendix
adjudication_rationale: The realized design is exactly 56 trajectories. Appendix F retains no-valid-output, submission failure, timeout and memory-error states, satisfying complete initiated-unit accounting.

adjudication_anchor: Introduction and §4/Fig. 3: 4,717 conjectures attempted, 1,050 claimed resolutions, 598 judge passes and 77 graded artifacts
adjudication_rationale: The target is the discovery funnel. All 4,717 attemptable conjectures receive the broad attempt and the subsequent counts are explicitly reconciled through the funnel. Expert review of only 15 affects R2/R3, not completeness of the initial denominator.

adjudication_anchor: §3.4 evaluation protocol and Appendix F.7 error handling; 7 tasks × 8 runs
adjudication_rationale: Each of the 56 runs follows the same development-selection-hidden-test protocol. Invalid or failed submissions receive explicit failure/capability outcomes rather than disappearing, so all initiated runs are covered under the stated narrow benchmark endpoint.

adjudication_anchor: §3.1 and §4.2: 1,773 explorations, 1,350 promising candidates, five architectures selected for 15B-token final validation
adjudication_rationale: Broad exploration assigns fitness, but the rigorous large-model/final-scale endpoint is applied only after outcome-conditioned filtering to five top architectures. This is structured but selected coverage, which the codebook defines as partial.

adjudication_anchor: Table 1 and §2.2 per-attempt case studies; Table 2 conference review for the successful manuscript
adjudication_rationale: All four selected ideas have recorded outcomes, but three are stopped under execution/evaluation judgments whereas only the successful manuscript receives conference-style review. The endpoint standards differ materially across initiated ideas, supporting partial rather than yes or no.

adjudication_anchor: Benchmark evaluation protocol and task-specific host metrics; Table 3
adjudication_rationale: For the explicitly narrow improvement-threshold target, fixed host-side task evaluators and held-out metrics are prespecified and separated from agent generation. Executable narrow-task tests may satisfy R3 even though they do not establish broader scientific validity.

adjudication_anchor: §3 annotation workflow, Fig. 4 and Appendix manual annotation: human experts build tests from original implementations; random 40-paper subset triple-annotated
adjudication_rationale: The unit tests are produced by experts separately from the evaluated reproduction agents and are checked on a human-annotated subset. However, they remain author-curated benchmark artifacts and full independent human adjudication does not cover all 168 runs, so independence is partial.

adjudication_anchor: §3 dataset/evaluation overview and Fig. 1; task descriptions in Appendix F
adjudication_rationale: AstaBench aggregates heterogeneous references: some tasks use fixed executable or gold-answer evaluators, while others rely on study-built rubrics and LLM judging without external calibration. The aggregate suite therefore combines independent and internal components, supporting partial.

adjudication_anchor: Methods around lines 248–286 and §5.5/Appendix B.4: three independent expert reviewers, blinded arms, prespecified rubric
adjudication_rationale: Every main run is assessed by three expert reviewers who are separated from run generation and blinded to experimental arm. The prespecified rubric and substantial inter-rater agreement provide sufficient procedural independence under R3.

adjudication_anchor: §3.1–3.3: expert taxonomy development, stratified 50-trajectory IAA sample, Agent-as-a-Judge scaling to 800 trajectories
adjudication_rationale: Three experts independently label only a stratified 50-trajectory calibration subset; an author-built agent judge then labels the full 800. This combines independent human evidence with internal scaled adjudication and therefore meets partial, not yes.

adjudication_anchor: §3.2 unit-test construction and Fig. 4; conclusion describing code reproducibility
adjudication_rationale: Unit tests directly assess correctness of key reproduced functions and consistency with the paper's implementation logic. That is an important reproducibility-validity dimension, but it does not reproduce or validate the full scientific result and conclusion, matching the codebook's partial category.

adjudication_anchor: §3.1 fitness function and §4.2 final validation: loss, benchmark score and LLM novelty/quality judgment
adjudication_rationale: The measured endpoint is composite fitness and selected language-model benchmark performance, including LLM-judge components. These establish optimization/task performance, not substantive validity of a scientific claim or discovery, so R4 is no.

adjudication_anchor: Table 1; §2.2 per-attempt implementation/evaluation case studies; Table 2 external review of the completed paper
adjudication_rationale: The target is idea-level completion and failure. The paper directly determines whether each idea produced executable, evaluable scientific evidence, documents scientific and implementation failure causes, and subjects the completed artifact to substantive review. Different coverage standards affect R2, not alignment of these endpoints with scientific validity.

adjudication_anchor: Introduction and §3 dataset construction; Fig. 1 and §4 evaluation of 92 real discrepancies
adjudication_rationale: Detecting ascertained paper–code discrepancies measures reproducibility and semantic consistency, a genuine validity dimension. It does not establish the full correctness of each paper's scientific conclusions, and the codebook explicitly places paper–code consistency in partial.

adjudication_anchor: §3.1 experimental setup and statistical test; lines 89–120; 800 independently replicated retrospective campaigns
adjudication_rationale: For the stated narrow target, a hit is whether a selected gene knockout has a statistically significant effect on the specified morphology feature in real JUMP perturbation data. This assay-aligned empirical endpoint directly measures the claimed gene–phenotype effect; retrospective simulation limits prospectiveness, not endpoint alignment.
